solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Black cask contains blue weapon

indicators.note: a thing that contains another holds it inside, so the blue word sits within the black-and-cask pair

blocks.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
feeling blue is feeling low
a pipe is a large cask for wine

explanation.surface: A black barrel holds something blue, which turns out to be a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Black and cask together form the container, with blue slipped in right after the first letter. A pipe is an old cask holding wine or port.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe is a tube through which a dart is blown, a hunting weapon.

clue.text: Reliable person with weapon outside Polish buildings

blocks.note: a brick is a dependable, good-hearted person
to sand something is to smooth or polish it
a mortar is a short cannon firing shells at high angles

explanation.surface: A dependable armed person surrounds Polish buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' places the weapon after, or below in this down light, the polish word. 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks and mortar is the idiom for buildings or property as a physical asset.

clue.text: Die Meistersinger is one work taking a long time

blocks.note: op. is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Wagner's Die Meistersinger is famously a work that takes a very long time to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' joins the second piece on after the first. The definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Die Meistersinger von Nürnberg is Wagner's comic opera, notoriously over four hours long.

clue.text: Alien is a hit, turning over unwanted guest

indicators.note: turning over flips something round, so the gathered words are read from the end

blocks.note: E.T. is Spielberg's extra-terrestrial
taken as written
a rap is a sharp blow

explanation.surface: An alien film is a box-office hit, about a visitor who won't leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite is someone who lives off others, like a guest who outstays their welcome.

clue.text: Quickly buy about fifty maps

indicators.note: about means around, so the buying word goes around the numeral

blocks.note: to buy quickly is to snap up; in a down light, 'snap up' means the word snap written upwards
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone grabs about fifty maps in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is the hidden phrase 'snap up': in a down clue, up turns the word over.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans are drawings of a site or building from above, a kind of map.

clue.text: Clobber retired doctor with a club

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the following words are read in the backward direction

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
a bat is a club used in sport

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to attack a retired doctor with a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like the verb 'hit', but it is British slang for clothes, the definition. 'Retired' turns back the whole of doctor, a and club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, an item of clothing, which clobber means in British slang.

clue.text: Help member of strings gives if missing intro

indicators.note: missing its intro means the opening letter of the player's word is dropped

blocks.note: a bassist plays the double bass in the string section

explanation.surface: An orchestral string player helps out when the introduction is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Some stars, together with lawyer, touring foreign city

indicators.note: to tour is to travel all round a place, so the outer words surround the city

blocks.note: and joins things together
the Italian capital
a DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: Some celebrities travel abroad with their lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like celebrities but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a northern constellation, a group of stars, also home to the Andromeda galaxy.

clue.text: Repeat novel in speech and end up receiving feasible complaint

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is spelt to sound like the novel synonym
in a down light, up means written from the bottom, so the word runs backwards
receiving means taking in, so the reversed word holds the next one inside

blocks.note: to double is to do again
novel means new, and the p in pneu is silent
an end is an aim or goal
on means practicable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Someone repeats a novel aloud and ends up catching a believable illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed MIA takes ON after its M. Pneumonia's silent P makes its start sound like 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, and double pneumonia is inflammation of both lungs.

clue.text: Tire out an Ox – one for a Japanese dish

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a yak is a Himalayan ox
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wearing out an ox, one swapped for a Japanese dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese dish of meat or fish glazed with a sweet soy marinade and grilled.

clue.text: I join beak and judge to imprison a drunk

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock inside, so the judge word surrounds the following letter

blocks.note: taken as written
neb is a Scottish and northern word for a beak or nose
to rate something is to judge it
a means one, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man joins a magistrate and a judge in locking up a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is British slang for a magistrate, which pulls toward a court scene; here it is a bird's bill. Reading 'a' as one, the Roman I, is a stretch the setter relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a habitual drunkard, the noun matching 'a drunk'.

clue.text: Holy man starts to use his drum and sitar to reflect

indicators.note: starts means beginnings, so each of the following words gives only its opening letter
a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the gathered letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the initial letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A holy man begins to play his drum and sitar for quiet contemplation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To reflect' looks like meditation, apt for a holy man, but it is the signal to turn the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic or wandering holy man in India.

clue.text: Loach movie brought round for poet

indicators.note: brought round means placed so as to encircle, so the film title wraps around the next word

blocks.note: Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and a kestrel
for in the price sense: selling for a pound is selling at a pound

explanation.surface: A Ken Loach film is revived or brought back into circulation, for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Loach is a British film director; Kes is his best-known film. 'For' looks like a link word but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, author of the great odes.

clue.text: Briefly move in the water and turn round ship? It's a piece of cake!

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for moving in water loses its final letter

blocks.note: to swim is to move through water
SS is short for steamship
to roll is to turn over and over, as a ship does in a swell

explanation.surface: A seaside outing ends with an easy swim and a boat ride, all no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like the idiom for something easy, which suits the jaunty surface, but it is literal: the answer is a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a sponge cake spread with jam and rolled up, so a slice is literally a piece of cake.

clue.text: Nob quietly leaves capital to conservative villain

indicators.note: when something leaves it departs, so the quiet letter drops out of the capital

blocks.note: the capital of France
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a rat is a contemptible person, a villain

explanation.surface: A posh person slips away from the city, leaving it to a Tory scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nob is British slang for a person of wealth or high social rank, which an aristocrat is.

clue.text: An insect's work is never-ending

indicators.note: work here means to work over or knead, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An insect's labour, like the ant's or bee's, never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause, which is never-ending.

clue.text: Arrest one in jail primarily smoking this?

definitions.text: Arrest one in jail primarily smoking this?

indicators.note: in places the first words within the jail word
primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: can is slang for prison
to nab is to catch or arrest
Roman numeral one
the first letter

explanation.surface: Asks what would get someone arrested and locked up for smoking it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, a substance you could be arrested for smoking; the question mark marks it as a loose &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is an illegal drug whose possession and smoking can lead to arrest and prison.

clue.text: Maintain a dungeon

blocks.note: first meaning: to look after or preserve something
second meaning: the strong central tower of a castle, the donjon

explanation.walkthrough: Dungeon and donjon are the same word; the castle keep is its older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep is both a verb for maintaining something and a noun for a castle's fortified main tower.

clue.text: Prisoner has to wait on husband

blocks.note: con is short for convict
to wait on someone is to serve them

explanation.surface: A convict must wait on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to manage thriftily.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them sparingly, which is to conserve them.

clue.text: Take pay from harbour

blocks.note: first meaning: to deduct money from someone's wages
second meaning: an enclosed area of water where ships moor

explanation.surface: Someone takes their wages away from the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages is to cut them; a dock is also a basin in a port where ships berth.

clue.text: Liven up rehashed rigatoni and serve regularly

indicators.note: rehashed food is cooked up again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged
regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Reheated pasta, served at intervals, is meant to perk diners up.
explanation.definitionFit: To invigorate is to give energy and vitality, synonymous with livening up.

clue.text: Start to make call in church

indicators.note: in places the calling word within the church abbreviation

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A phone call made during a church service is the start of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' looks like 'begin' but means to jump in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to flinch or recoil suddenly, which is what cringing involves.

clue.text: Old boy's valet is alert

blocks.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
a valet is a personal manservant

explanation.surface: A former pupil's manservant is said to be on the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has': the old boy has a valet next to him, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Being observant means noticing things quickly, the same as being alert.

clue.text: Outdo partially sincere politician?

indicators.note: partially means only in part, so the honest word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a true friend is a sincere one
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Asks whether a politician can be only partly sincere.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark nods to a famous politician of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to beat or outdo, from playing a trump card.

clue.text: Journalist has problem about plant

indicators.note: the problem word has, that is holds, the journalist inside it

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter has trouble writing about a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedum is a genus of succulent plants, the stonecrops, common in rock gardens.

clue.text: Miserable and extremely obese author

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are taken

blocks.note: miserable is fed up, and in a down light 'fed up' means fed written upwards
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A writer is described as unhappy and very fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe. As in 4 down, a hidden 'up' turns a word over in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was an English author, best known for Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Coach some of them?

blocks.note: surface reading: to coach is to instruct, as a sports instructor does
setter's reading: railway carriages are coaches, and several of them strung together make up a locomotive-hauled vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense gives the answer directly; the question mark covers the joke that the same answer is a thing made of coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to coach them, and a railway train is a line of coaches.

clue.text: I burp horribly and often – no time for medicine

indicators.note: something done horribly is done in a mess, so the letters are jumbled
no time means a removal of the time abbreviation from the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sufferer belching often admits they have had no time to take their pills.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from OFTEN before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling, anti-inflammatory drug, a medicine sold over the counter.

clue.text: A bit sooner

blocks.note: first meaning: somewhat, as in a bit cold
second meaning: preferably, as in I would sooner go

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a bit sooner' as earlier; the clue is two separate adverbs instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather means somewhat (rather cold) and also preferably (I'd rather stay).

clue.text: There's harm done with epee but it won't last long

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: things of fleeting interest

indicators.note: harm done is damage inflicted, and something done over is reworked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fencing injury inflicted with an epee will soon heal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that are short-lived or of only passing interest, which by nature do not endure.
